record.what_it_does: Cloud accounting software for small businesses: invoicing, bank feeds, payroll, reporting.
record.auth_notes: Every API request goes through Xero's OAuth 2.0 gateway. Multi-user apps use the authorization code flow, with PKCE also supported (the Remote MCP FAQ confirms PKCE). Custom Connections use the OAuth 2.0 client_credentials grant and work for a single organisation only, so they are a variant of OAuth 2.0 rather than a separate method. I found no API keys or personal access tokens. Webhook payloads are signed with an HMAC in the x-xero-signature header, but that covers webhook verification, not API auth. The developer.xero.com OAuth pages are rendered client-side and returned no body text, so I took the auth evidence from Xero's official xero-node SDK README.
record.access_notes: Any developer can create an app on the free Starter tier: up to 5 connections, no charge, no payment method, and 1,000 calls per day per organisation. Core (A$35/mo, 50 connections), Plus (A$245, 1,000), Advanced (A$1,445, 10,000) and Enterprise (price on application) require a registered credit card. App Certification and a Security Assessment (initial and annual) are listed as prerequisites, but the page text does not map them cleanly to tiers. App Store listing is not applicable on Starter and Core, optional on Plus and Advanced, and required on Enterprise. The Journal endpoint, the XPM API and Bulk Connections need a security assessment and use-case approval. Xero's official Remote MCP is included on Core and above; Starter apps can only use it with the demo organisation.
record.api_breadth_notes: Xero publishes OpenAPI 3.0 specs for Accounting, Identity, Bank Feeds, Fixed Assets, Projects, Payroll AU, Payroll UK, Payroll NZ and Files. The repo also holds specs for Finance, App Store, Account Data and Webhooks. The official SDK claims "full method coverage" for the Accounting, Assets, Bankfeeds, Files, Projects and Payroll (AU, NZ, UK) API sets. I did not count operations exactly, but the Accounting API alone covers invoices, contacts, payments, bank transactions, accounts, journals, quotes, credit notes, items, tracking and reports, which is well over 50 operations.
record.mcp_notes: Xero hosts an official Developer Remote MCP at https://api.xero.com/mcp/v1. It authenticates with OAuth 2.0 plus PKCE, reads and writes Xero data, and is included on Core and above (Starter apps get the demo organisation only). Xero also publishes a local server, XeroAPI/xero-mcp-server (MIT, npm @xeroapi/xero-mcp-server, 51 tools), which authenticates with either a Custom Connection or a bearer token. A directory lists a separate endpoint, mcp.xero.com/mcp, but I could not confirm it on Xero's own site.
record.blocker_notes: Building and testing are free on Starter, but Starter caps an app at 5 connected organisations and 1,000 calls per day per organisation. Serving many end users needs Core (A$35/mo, 50 connections) or higher. That means a credit card, egress billing (A$2.40/GB over the allotment), and, at higher tiers, App Certification and an annual Security Assessment. Core and above allow 5,000 calls per day per organisation. Some premium endpoints (Journals, XPM, Bulk Connections) need extra approval.
